title: Beal Conjecture — Tate Local Conductor Verification — v4.1.0
description: v4.1.0 Tate Local Conductor Verification. This release makes the Tate boundary truthful about which local data are being supplied and why. The closed B14 work defines the Frey Weierstrass invariants b2, b4, c4, and discriminant, proves the c4 identity by ring normalization, and proves the odd-prime c4 nonvanishing cases used by the local argument. A typed FreyCurveModel keeps the coefficients, c4, discriminant, conductor, prime support, and local conductor relation tied to one fixed tuple (A, B, C, x, y, z). The derived tate_frey_multiplicative theorem chooses that one model and returns its actual conductor rather than an unrelated natural-number witness. The remaining named Tate boundary is Beal.FreyTate.TateStep2.tate_step2_I_n_conductor_one, an explicit local axiom corresponding to the supplied odd-prime Tate Step 2 contract. This does not formalize the full Tate algorithm, the 2-adic conductor exponent, or a global conductor computation from coefficients. In the active B14-B20 path, the three named mathematical boundaries are Tate, Wiles modularity, and typed preserved-form Ribet descent; Lean foundation dependencies are audited separately. No executable sorry or sorryAx is claimed or used in the active path.
